name: Readmission to Ethiopian Citizenship (former citizens)

qualifying_event.description: A former Ethiopian national who acquired a foreign nationality may seek readmission to Ethiopian citizenship by returning to Ethiopia, renouncing the foreign nationality, and applying to the authorities. Consistent with Ethiopia's no-dual-citizenship rule, readmission requires giving up the other nationality -- it is not a route to holding both.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Documentation of prior Ethiopian nationality and its loss; proof of renunciation of the foreign nationality.

requirements.blocker_text: Previously held Ethiopian citizenship and lost it by acquiring a foreign nationality.
Must renounce the foreign nationality as a condition of readmission -- Ethiopia does not permit dual citizenship.

evidence_required.document: Documentation of prior Ethiopian citizenship and its loss
Proof of renunciation of the foreign nationality

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: return to Ethiopia required as part of the readmission process

sources.title: African Child Policy Forum (hosting the full text) -- Ethiopian Nationality Proclamation No. 378/2003: readmission provision for former Ethiopian nationals who acquired foreign nationality, conditioned on renouncing the foreign nationality

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Ethiopia). STATUS: DRAFT -- same tier-2 sourcing caveat as the other Ethiopian citizenship files. WORTH CONTRASTING WITH et_ancestry_origin_id.json: readmission is the harder, ALL-OR-NOTHING path back to actual citizenship (requires giving up the foreign nationality entirely), while the Yellow Card is the softer, dual-status-compatible alternative most of the diaspora actually uses in practice -- this file exists for completeness of the legal picture, but the Yellow Card route is very likely the more commonly used instrument given it doesn't force a choice between nationalities. No fee, processing time, or residency-duration-before-application detail was found for this specific readmission route beyond 'returning to Ethiopia and applying.'
